title: Instruction-based Time Series Editing

problem.claim: Time series editing seeks to modify selected properties of a time series while preserving others.

gap.claim: Existing diffusion-based editors use rigid predefined attribute-vector conditions, produce all-or-nothing edits through sampling, limit condition-format flexibility, and lack customizable editing-strength control.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces instruction-based time series editing, allowing users to specify intended edits with natural language.
The paper introduces InstructTime, which embeds time series and instructions into a shared multimodal representation space and decodes them into edited time series.
The approach uses embedding interpolation for varying edit strength and multi-resolution encoders for local and global edits.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In experiments on synthetic and real datasets, the authors report that InstructTime achieves high-quality edits with controllable strength.
The authors report that InstructTime can generalize to unseen instructions.
The authors report that InstructTime can be adapted to unseen conditions through few-shot learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: The task is to edit selected properties of a time series while preserving other properties.
Existing diffusion-based editors impose rigid attribute-vector conditions and sampling-based all-or-nothing edits, limiting flexibility and edit-strength control.
The paper proposes specifying intended time series edits through natural-language instructions.
InstructTime jointly represents time series and instructions, interpolates embeddings for adjustable edit strength, and uses multi-resolution encoders for local and global edits.
Experiments on synthetic and real datasets are reported to show high-quality controllable edits, generalization to unseen instructions, and few-shot adaptation to unseen conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, baselines, dataset names, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, instruction data, or few-shot adaptation protocol.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported state-of-the-art claim.
